passages.title: The History of Tea
passages.text:
Tea is one of the most widely consumed beverages in the world, second only to water. Its origins can be traced back thousands of years to ancient China, where it was first used for medicinal purposes before becoming a popular drink.
Legend attributes the discovery of tea to Emperor Shen Nong, who is said to have accidentally discovered the beverage when tea leaves blew into a pot of boiling water. Whether or not this story is historically accurate, archaeological evidence confirms that tea cultivation in China dates back at least to the Han Dynasty.
Tea spread to Japan through Buddhist monks who studied in China and brought both tea plants and the ceremonial practices associated with tea drinking back to their homeland. This eventually evolved into the elaborate Japanese tea ceremony still practised today.
In the 17th century, tea was introduced to Europe by Portuguese and Dutch traders. It quickly became a fashionable drink among the European aristocracy before becoming widely accessible to the general population. Britain, in particular, developed a strong tea culture, which later spread to its colonies, including India, where the British established extensive tea plantations in the 19th century.
